code: case class Item(name: String, price: BigDecimal, qty: Int)

frames.title: Open the file
frames.caption: Opening the file is a write action: a new run whose top-level statements are entered but not typed. Every symbol is still lazy.

T3: write action: enter the new text, skip every statement

frames.title: The background pass starts
frames.caption: T2 types from the top with its own Reader. It claims each completion root before completing it; while it runs, the symbol's info is an InProgress that only T2 can see through. Line 9 holds T2 inside subtotal, so every run interleaves the same way.

note.text: holds the typer here, so every run interleaves the same way

frames.title: Hover on total
frames.caption: T1 types only the path to total. total's inferred type needs subtotal's. T1 takes the slow path that every LazyType already takes, finds the root claimed by T2, and waits on the claim. It never sees T2's half-built state, and never mistakes "in progress elsewhere" for a cycle.

T1: needs subtotal: waits on T2's claim

frames.title: T2 publishes subtotal
frames.caption: Released from line 9, T2 finishes subtotal. The info is published before the claim is released, so T1 wakes to a complete denotation. T1 needs tax next, which T2 has just claimed: a second, short wait.

T1: needs tax: waits on T2's claim

frames.title: The hover answers
frames.caption: T1 completes total and answers BigDecimal, the answer a single reader gives. It typed only what the hover needed: receipt stays skipped.

frames.title: The background pass finishes
frames.caption: T2 reaches Checkout, finds total already published by T1, and types the receipt that T1 skipped. Every statement is typed; no diagnostics.

frames.title: A keystroke in receipt, nothing in flight
frames.caption: The edit only touches receipt's body. The write action re-indexes receipt and keeps the run: every other symbol stays published.

frames.title: The hover after the edit
frames.caption: T3's request types line 19 and nothing else, reading subtotal, tax and total as already published.

frames.title: The same keystroke, while T2 is held
frames.caption: Back to the moment T1 waits on T2. Now the user types in receipt. The editor cancels the stale hover and pass, and the new text arrives as a writer. The writer raises a sticky cancel and waits for the readers to leave.

T3: write pending: waits for the readers to leave

frames.title: T2 unwinds
frames.caption: At its next checkpoint T2 unwinds. It resets the roots it was completing and releases the claim. A Namer completion cannot run twice, so subtotal is left marked as unwound rather than lazy.

T2: cancelled: reset subtotal, released the claim

frames.title: The waiter takes over, and is pre-empted
frames.caption: T1 now owns subtotal's root and meets the unwound completion. It cannot finish it, so it is pre-empted: it resets total, unwinds, and the run is tainted. No hang, no torn state; the work is just not reused.

frames.title: A fresh run for the new text
frames.caption: The writer installs the new text in a fresh run. T3 types receipt, completing total, subtotal and tax along the way, and answers. The background pass on the new text follows in the same run.

frames.title: Two readers, one lazy symbol
frames.caption: Take away the claims. T2 is completing subtotal, whose inferred type needs its body typed. In a compiler with one thread, a symbol whose completion has started and not finished is somewhere on the current call stack.

frames.title: The other reader concludes there is a cycle
frames.caption: T1 needs subtotal's type and finds its completion under way. With one thread that can only mean a cycle, so T1 reports one: a false error in the editor. Had it looked through the completer instead, it would have read T2's half-built state.

T1: reports a cycle that is not there

popup.text: Overloaded or recursive method subtotal needs return type

frames.title: Claim the root
frames.caption: Before completing, T2 claims subtotal's completion root and sets its info to an InProgress: a lazy type that records T2 as its owner. Only T2 sees through it, to the info it is building.

frames.title: Wait, don't peek
frames.caption: To T1 the InProgress is a lazy type like any other, so it takes the slow path every unforced symbol already takes. There it finds the root claimed by another reader and waits on the claim. Asking whether subtotal is completing waits in the same way, instead of answering from a glimpse.

frames.title: Publish, release, wake
frames.caption: T2 publishes the info, then releases the claim. T1 wakes, reads the finished type and answers BigDecimal, as one reader would.

frames.title: A shared reference caches what it resolved to
frames.caption: Types are shared by all readers, and a reference such as subtotal in total's body caches what it resolved to: a denotation, a symbol, and the period they were checked in. T2 resolves it and stores the three, in that order, with plain stores.

frames.title: Seen in another order
frames.caption: On Apple silicon, plain stores can become visible to another thread in a different order. T1 finds the period current, trusts the cached fields, and gets a null symbol. This was seen in testing.

frames.title: The period publishes the fields
frames.caption: The period is the flag that publishes the other fields. T2 stores the denotation and the symbol, then the period with a release store. T1 loads the period with an acquire load.

frames.title: Current means complete
frames.caption: If T1 finds the period current, it sees everything stored before it; if not, it resolves the reference itself. Either way the symbol is never null. On x86 an acquire load is a plain load.

frames.title: A value and its stamp, in two fields
frames.caption: Many caches keep a value and the period it was computed in, as two plain fields: here, the supertype of List[Item]. The previous run left both behind. In run 2, T2 computes the value again and stores the value, then the period.

heap.title: List[Item]: a cache in two fields

frames.title: A torn pair
frames.caption: T1 sees the new period beside the old value, so the hit hands it a type built in the previous run. Two writers in one period can also leave one's stamp beside the other's value. Seen in testing: a null, a false, the previous run's value.

heap.title: List[Item]: a cache in two fields

frames.title: One field, one immutable pair
frames.caption: The cache becomes one field holding a Stamped: the stamp and the value together, in an immutable object whose fields are final. A miss computes the value and replaces the whole pair.

frames.title: Old or new, never mixed
frames.caption: T1 loads the reference once and sees one pair whole: the new one, a hit, or the old one, a miss it computes again. No fences, and the same code with one thread or several. The price is an allocation per miss.

frames.title: A keystroke behind a long pass
frames.caption: T2's background pass holds a read lock while it types. The user types in receipt. With a plain read/write lock the writer waits for the whole pass, which on a large file takes seconds, and every keystroke after it waits too.

T3: waits for the pass to end

frames.title: The writer is pending
frames.caption: Instead, the writer raises a pending flag and queues for the lock; readers that start now queue behind it. T2 polls the flag at its typer checkpoints, unwinds at the next one, and releases the read lock.

T3: pending: waits for readers to leave

frames.title: The writer runs alone
frames.caption: With no reader left, the writer takes the lock and applies the edit: the change is inside receipt's body, so it re-indexes receipt and keeps the run.

frames.title: Readers are retried
frames.caption: The writer releases the lock. T2's request is retried on the new text, and its caller never sees the cancellation. A writer waits only until each reader reaches its next checkpoint, and no reader sees a write half done.

frames.title: The owner is cancelled
frames.caption: T2 is completing subtotal, and T1 waits on its claim. The user types, and T2 is cancelled in the middle of the completion.

frames.title: What a careless unwind leaves
frames.caption: If T2 simply unwound, subtotal would keep an InProgress that nobody is completing, or the half-built info T2 had set. T1 would wait forever, or read the half-built info.

T1: on a claim nobody will finish

frames.title: Reset, then release
frames.caption: Unwinding, T2 resets every root it was completing before it releases the claims. A Namer completion cannot run twice, because it changes the trees it types, so subtotal is left marked as an unwound completion rather than as lazy.

frames.title: The waiter takes over, and is pre-empted
frames.caption: T1 takes the claim over and meets the unwound completion. It cannot finish it, so it is pre-empted too: it resets total, unwinds, and the run is marked tainted.

frames.title: A fresh run
frames.caption: The writer gives the new text a fresh run, and the next request completes subtotal from scratch. No reader waits on work that nobody is doing, and none reads a half-built info. What it costs is the run.
